## godot_resources

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_resources")

godot_resources(<a href="#godot_resources-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_resources-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_resources-srcs">srcs</a>, <a href="#godot_resources-import_inputs">import_inputs</a>, <a href="#godot_resources-prefix">prefix</a>, <a href="#godot_resources-resource_paths">resource_paths</a>, <a href="#godot_resources-runtime_deps">runtime_deps</a>,
                <a href="#godot_resources-runtime_references">runtime_references</a>, <a href="#godot_resources-strip_prefix">strip_prefix</a>)
</pre>

Declare Godot resources as one import unit, imported under the project of each
operation that reaches them.

Produces GodotResourcesInfo and DefaultInfo. Under the project an operation names,
the target imports its own files once per project and target platform, after its
dependencies; outside every operation it imports nothing. deps and runtime_deps
become members of the operations that reach them, and the add-ons in deps come
with them; import_inputs are available only during import. Conflicting resource
paths fail. Under each project, a validation in the _validation output group loads
the target's own scripts and scenes with what deps bring, and every build containing
the target fails on the errors Godot reports. Autoloads, settings, extensions and platform libraries are declared on
the project or a godot_addon, never on resources.

Example:
```starlark
godot_resources(name = "textures", srcs = glob(["textures/**"]))
```

See [resource composition](../../resources.md) for resource paths, generated
files, import ordering and runtime reference cycles.

### Default outputs
- files (many): build declared resource files; no run behavior

**ATTRIBUTES**


| Name  | Description | Type | Mandatory | Default |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_resources-name"></a>name |  A unique name for this target.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels#target-names">Name</a> | required |  |
| <a id="godot_resources-deps"></a>deps |  What these resources use: other godot_resources, which become members of the same operations and are imported first, and the add-ons their files use, godot_addon, godot_extension and godot_cc_extension targets. Every operation containing these resources contains those add-ons with their autoloads, settings, extensions and platform libraries; an add-on's files are never an input of this import. Platform libraries, autoloads, settings and Info.plist fragments belong on a godot_addon.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `[]`  |
| <a id="godot_resources-srcs"></a>srcs |  Source or generated files of these resources, from any package or repository; each file's path is relative to the package of the target that lists it, after strip_prefix.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `[]`  |
| <a id="godot_resources-import_inputs"></a>import_inputs |  Files this import reads that are no members of any operation, such as a glTF's buffers or a scene import's post-import script; scripts and scenes reach an import only this way.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `[]`  |

<a id="godot_editor"></a>

## godot_editor

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_editor")

godot_editor(<a href="#godot_editor-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_editor-project">project</a>, <a href="#godot_editor-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_editor-env">env</a>, <a href="#godot_editor-write_sidecars">write_sidecars</a>, <a href="#godot_editor-kwargs">**kwargs</a>)
</pre>

Open a project in the Godot editor with `bazel run`, editing the checkout.

The editor view is a Godot project under `.godot-editor/<package>/<name>` in the
workspace. Its files from this repository are symbolic links into the
checkout, so what the editor saves changes the checkout. A directory whose
files all come from one checkout directory at the same relative paths is
linked as a whole, so files the editor creates, renames or deletes there
change the checkout too. Generated files, files of other repositories, such
as add-ons, and extension descriptors and libraries are read-only copies;
the editor loads the extension host editor libraries. The project's imports and
Godot's caches come from the build, so the editor opens without
reimporting. Before the editor opens, the run writes the sidecars the
checkout lacks, as godot_metadata_sync does.

The editor view holds the editor part of every add-on of the operation, with its
editor plugin enabled in the view's project.godot. When the editor exits, settings
it changed that come from the authored project.godot are written back to it;
settings the project or its add-ons set are reported with the label that sets them. The runner also
lists files that exist only in the editor view and files in linked directories that
the project does not declare.

Bazel must ignore the editor views: add `.godot-editor` to `.bazelignore`, or
`bazel build //...` finds the linked packages twice. The run fails until it
does. Arguments after `--` go to the editor.

Example:
```starlark
godot_editor(
    name = "edit",
    project = ":project",
    deps = [":game"],
)
```

`bazel run :edit` opens the editor on `.godot-editor/<package>/edit`.

### Default outputs
- executable (one): run an editable staged project in Godot; editor and project are runfiles


**PARAMETERS**


| Name  | Description | Default Value |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_editor-name"></a>name |  Name of the executable target.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_editor-project"></a>project |  The godot_project whose configuration the editor view uses.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_editor-deps"></a>deps |  What the editor view lists for editing: godot_resources and add-ons, as an IDE project view lists targets.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_editor-env"></a>env |  Environment variables set for the editor, besides the user's own.   |  `{}` |
| <a id="godot_editor-write_sidecars"></a>write_sidecars |  Write the sidecars the checkout lacks before the editor opens, as godot_metadata_sync does. Without it, the run names them and Godot writes its own when it finds the files, reimporting assets.   |  `True` |
| <a id="godot_editor-kwargs"></a>kwargs |  Common attributes, such as tags and visibility.   |  none |


<a id="godot_metadata_sync"></a>

## godot_metadata_sync

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_metadata_sync")

godot_metadata_sync(<a href="#godot_metadata_sync-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_metadata_sync-project">project</a>, <a href="#godot_metadata_sync-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_metadata_sync-size">size</a>, <a href="#godot_metadata_sync-timeout">timeout</a>, <a href="#godot_metadata_sync-kwargs">**kwargs</a>)
</pre>

Write the metadata Godot keeps beside a project's checkout files, and test for it.

Godot keeps a script's or shader's UID in a `.uid` file beside it and an
imported asset's import settings, including its UID, in a `.import` file
beside it; both belong in version control. Where a checkout file has none,
the build generates them. `bazel run :<name>` writes those beside their
files in the checkout, where none exists yet, and names the target to
declare each in: commit them and declare them there, which a `glob` does on
its own. Existing files are never replaced; the run names the ones that
exist but are not declared.

With `--@autoload_rules_godot//godot/metadata:node_ids` or
`--@autoload_rules_godot//godot/metadata:resource_uids` at `sync` (default) or
`require`, the run also adds the `unique_id` each node of a checkout `.tscn`
scene lacks and the named file's UID to each `ext_resource` of a `.tscn` or
`.tres` file whose `uid` is missing or stale: the values a pack otherwise
adds only to the copy it exports.

`<name>.test` fails while the build generates a sidecar for a checkout file
and, for a metadata flag at `require`, while a file lacks those values, so
`bazel test //...` keeps the checkout complete. It needs no checkout and
names each sidecar with the command that writes it.

Example:
```starlark
godot_metadata_sync(
    name = "metadata",
    project = ":project",
    deps = [":game"],
)
```

### Default outputs
- executable (one): run writes missing metadata to the checkout; editor/project runfiles

### Generated targets
- `{name}.test` (test): Execute missing-metadata validation as a Bazel test; an output group cannot execute tests
  - purpose: test
  - visibility: caller
  - testonly: true
  - prerequisites: project imports and execution-platform editor


**PARAMETERS**


| Name  | Description | Default Value |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_metadata_sync-name"></a>name |  Name of the writer; the test is `<name>.test`.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_metadata_sync-project"></a>project |  The godot_project whose configuration the files are read under.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_metadata_sync-deps"></a>deps |  The godot_resources whose checkout files get their metadata.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_metadata_sync-size"></a>size |  Bazel test size of `<name>.test`; Bazel's default applies when unset.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_metadata_sync-timeout"></a>timeout |  Bazel test timeout of `<name>.test`; derived from size when unset.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_metadata_sync-kwargs"></a>kwargs |  Common attributes of both targets, such as tags and visibility.   |  none |

## godot_run

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_run")

godot_run(<a href="#godot_run-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_run-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_run-main">main</a>, <a href="#godot_run-project">project</a>, <a href="#godot_run-pack">pack</a>, <a href="#godot_run-data">data</a>, <a href="#godot_run-env">env</a>, <a href="#godot_run-headless">headless</a>, <a href="#godot_run-engine_errors">engine_errors</a>, <a href="#godot_run-additional_packs">additional_packs</a>,
          <a href="#godot_run-kwargs">**kwargs</a>)
</pre>

Run a Godot project or exported PCK with `bazel run`, like py_binary.

The run uses the registered editor toolchain in a fresh, writable copy of the
project, so nothing in the checkout changes. Give it what to run in one of
two ways: a project and the resources it runs in deps, or an exported pack. `args` are Godot's command line, which
Bazel splits like a shell; arguments for the running script follow Godot's `--`
separator.

Example:
```starlark
godot_run(
    name = "game",
    project = ":project",
    deps = [":main", ":assets"],
    headless = False,
)
```

`bazel run :game` opens the game's window. See
[execution and tests](../../development.md#execution-and-tests).

### Default outputs
- executable (one): run Godot with project or PCK; project and editor data are runfiles


**PARAMETERS**


| Name  | Description | Default Value |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_run-name"></a>name |  Name of the executable target.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_run-deps"></a>deps |  godot_resources and godot_extension targets the run contains, such as code, assets and add-ons. The project's autoloads and main scene must be among them.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_run-main"></a>main |  Resource path, with optional res:// prefix, of what Godot starts: a SceneTree or MainLoop script runs with --script, a .tscn or .scn scene replaces the main scene. Empty starts the project's main scene.   |  `""` |
| <a id="godot_run-project"></a>project |  The godot_project whose configuration the run uses; defaults to a minimal project.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_run-pack"></a>pack |  An exported godot_pack to run instead of a project.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_run-data"></a>data |  Files available at run time through runfiles, outside the Godot project. Godot receives Bazel's runfiles directory/manifest variables when set. Tests also receive TEST_SRCDIR and TEST_WORKSPACE for locating them.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_run-env"></a>env |  Environment variables set for Godot.   |  `{}` |
| <a id="godot_run-headless"></a>headless |  Whether Godot runs without a display: True always, False never, for a target that must render. Unset follows the --@autoload_rules_godot//godot:headless flag, which is true by default.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_run-engine_errors"></a>engine_errors |  "fail" or "report": what an error Godot reports while the game's tree exists, such as a script error, does to the run. Godot can report one and still exit with 0. "fail" ends the run with 1 instead; "report" keeps Godot's exit status. Either names the number of recorded errors.   |  `"fail"` |
| <a id="godot_run-additional_packs"></a>additional_packs |  Pack -> file name in the working directory, for the running project to load with ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack().   |  `{}` |
| <a id="godot_run-kwargs"></a>kwargs |  Common attributes such as args and visibility.   |  none |

## godot_test

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_test")

godot_test(<a href="#godot_test-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_test-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_test-main">main</a>, <a href="#godot_test-project">project</a>, <a href="#godot_test-pack">pack</a>, <a href="#godot_test-data">data</a>, <a href="#godot_test-env">env</a>, <a href="#godot_test-headless">headless</a>, <a href="#godot_test-engine_errors">engine_errors</a>, <a href="#godot_test-additional_packs">additional_packs</a>,
           <a href="#godot_test-kwargs">**kwargs</a>)
</pre>

Run a Godot project or exported PCK as a Bazel test, like py_test.

The test passes when Godot exits with 0, so a script reports a failed check
with `quit(1)`. Test frameworks run as the main script: autoload_gdunit's
gdunit_test sets up GdUnit this way. Godot receives Bazel's test environment,
such as TEST_SHARD_INDEX, TESTBRIDGE_TEST_ONLY and XML_OUTPUT_FILE, so a test
framework can implement sharding, `--test_filter` and JUnit reports. size, timeout,
shard_count and flaky work as for any Bazel test. The test and its view of the
project are testonly unless testonly = False is passed, so production
targets cannot depend on them.

Example:
```starlark
godot_test(
    name = "smoke_test",
    deps = [":smoke", ":game"],
    main = "smoke_test.gd",
)
```

Watch it with `bazel test :smoke_test --@autoload_rules_godot//godot:headless=false`.
See [execution and tests](../../development.md#execution-and-tests).

### Default outputs
- test (one): execute Godot under bazel test; failure follows the exit status and engine_errors; project/editor are runfiles


**PARAMETERS**


| Name  | Description | Default Value |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_test-name"></a>name |  Name of the test target.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_test-deps"></a>deps |  godot_resources and godot_extension targets the test contains: the test scripts and fixtures, the code under test, a test framework and its add-ons. Autoloads and a main scene of the project whose files are not among them are left out.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_test-main"></a>main |  Resource path, with optional res:// prefix, of what Godot starts: a SceneTree or MainLoop script runs with --script, a .tscn or .scn scene replaces the main scene. Empty starts the project's main scene.   |  `""` |
| <a id="godot_test-project"></a>project |  The godot_project whose configuration the test uses; defaults to a minimal project.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_test-pack"></a>pack |  An exported godot_pack to test instead of a project.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_test-data"></a>data |  Files available at run time through runfiles, outside the Godot project. Godot receives Bazel's runfiles directory/manifest variables when set. Tests also receive TEST_SRCDIR and TEST_WORKSPACE for locating them.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_test-env"></a>env |  Environment variables set for Godot.   |  `{}` |
| <a id="godot_test-headless"></a>headless |  Whether Godot runs without a display: True always, False never, for a test that must render. Unset follows the --@autoload_rules_godot//godot:headless flag, which is true by default.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_test-engine_errors"></a>engine_errors |  "fail" or "report": what an error Godot reports while the game's tree exists, such as a script error, does to the test. "fail" fails the test and stops it after the first error, since a script error does not end Godot; "report" keeps Godot's exit status, for a test framework that provokes errors on purpose. Either names the number of recorded errors; the errors are in the test's undeclared outputs under godot/errors.jsonl.   |  `"fail"` |

| <a id="godot_test-kwargs"></a>kwargs |  Common test attributes such as args, size and shard_count.   |  none |

## godot_addon

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_addon")

godot_addon(*, <a href="#godot_addon-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-srcs">srcs</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-autoloads">autoloads</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-deprecation">deprecation</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-directory">directory</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-editor_resource_paths">editor_resource_paths</a>,
            <a href="#godot_addon-editor_srcs">editor_srcs</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-exec_compatible_with">exec_compatible_with</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-exec_properties">exec_properties</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-features">features</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-import_settings">import_settings</a>,
            <a href="#godot_addon-importer_suffixes">importer_suffixes</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-infoplists">infoplists</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-platform_deps">platform_deps</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-resource_paths">resource_paths</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-settings">settings</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-strip_prefix">strip_prefix</a>,
            <a href="#godot_addon-tags">tags</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-target_compatible_with">target_compatible_with</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-testonly">testonly</a>, <a href="#godot_addon-visibility">visibility</a>)
</pre>

Declare an add-on once: its runtime part, its editor part with its roles, its
extensions, platform libraries, Info.plist fragments, autoloads, settings and the
add-ons it needs.

Resources whose files use the add-on list it in their deps; a project lists in its
deps the add-ons no content uses, such as an editor-only add-on, and every add-on
with importer_suffixes its content needs. Every operation containing those resources,
or of that project, contains the add-on: its runtime
part as members, its autoloads and settings merged into the configuration, its
extensions and platform libraries delivered by the applications shipping its packs.
The editor part is a tool: editor views load it, imports of files of its
importer_suffixes run it under a project that names the add-on, and no pack, source
run or application contains it. No export runs its EditorExportPlugin: what one adds
to Godot's own export is declared, as platform_deps, infoplists and pack settings.
Test-only resources that load its scripts, such as suites of its editor tooling, list
`<name>.editor` in their deps; that target is always test-only. A use
never makes the add-on's files inputs of the resources' import. Under the context of
an operation the add-on imports its parts itself, once per project and target
platform, whether content uses it or the project names it, and validates each part's
scripts and scenes as godot_resources validates its own.

Every file lives below directory, by default addons/<name>; srcs and editor_srcs
from any package or repository are placed there by their path relative to the
package of the listed target, after strip_prefix, and resource_paths and
editor_resource_paths at explicit paths. Two add-ons of one operation with overlapping
directories fail, as does a file in both parts.

Example:
```starlark
godot_addon(
    name = "inventory",
    srcs = glob(["runtime/**"]),
    editor_srcs = glob(["editor/**"]),
    autoloads = {"Inventory": "*res://addons/inventory/runtime/inventory.gd"},
    platform_deps = select({
        "@platforms//os:android": [":inventory_android"],
        "//conditions:default": [],
    }),
)

godot_resources(name = "shop", srcs = ["shop.gd"], deps = [":inventory"])
```

See [add-ons](../../resources.md#add-ons) and [importers](../../resources.md#importers).

### Default outputs
- files (many): build the files of both parts; no run behavior

### Generated targets
- `{name}.editor` (metadata): the editor part as resources of test-only operations, such as suites of its editor tooling, which products cannot reach
  - visibility: caller
  - testonly: true

| Name  | Description | Type | Mandatory | Default |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |

The names of any other targets that this macro might create will be this name with a string suffix.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels#target-names">Name</a> | required |  |
| <a id="godot_addon-deps"></a>deps |  The add-ons it needs and its extensions: godot_addon, godot_extension and godot_cc_extension targets. Every extension here is the add-on's, wherever its descriptor lies: the add-on's parts and importer load it. Every operation containing this add-on contains its extensions and the add-ons it needs. <a id="godot_pack"></a>

## godot_pack

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_pack")

godot_pack(*, <a href="#godot_pack-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-deprecation">deprecation</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-entry_points">entry_points</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-exec_compatible_with">exec_compatible_with</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-exec_properties">exec_properties</a>,
           <a href="#godot_pack-export_options">export_options</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-features">features</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-packing">packing</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-preset_settings">preset_settings</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-project">project</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-required_packs">required_packs</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-settings">settings</a>,
           <a href="#godot_pack-tags">tags</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-target_compatible_with">target_compatible_with</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-testonly">testonly</a>, <a href="#godot_pack-visibility">visibility</a>)
</pre>

Export a project as one PCK for the selected export platform.

The PCK contains extension descriptors, never extension libraries;
see [export membership](../../resources.md#export-membership).
Its extensions and platform libraries stay visible to the aspects of rules_android
and rules_apple in each platform slice. The export itself runs once, in the content
configuration, for all platform slices. Outside optimized builds the PCK is written
without Godot's conversions; see [pack forms](../../resources.md#pack-forms). DefaultInfo contains the PCK; GodotPackInfo
carries the project of each platform slice and the facts of the common export.
OutputGroupInfo.report exposes the export report. required_packs only affects which
files this pack contains; applications do not package the required packs, and
nothing mounts them at runtime.

Example: godot_pack(name = "pack", project = ":project", deps = [":game"]).
See [export behavior](../../resources.md).

### Default outputs
- files (one): build output_name.pck; no run behavior

### Output groups
- `report`: Godot export JSON report
  - prerequisites: execution-platform editor
- `export_facts`: What Godot reports about the export, as JSON
  - prerequisites: execution-platform editor
- `selection`: Selected content JSON and the selection's warnings

**ATTRIBUTES**


| Name  | Description | Type | Mandatory | Default |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_pack-name"></a>name |  A unique name for this macro instance. Normally, this is also the name for the macro's main or only target. The names of any other targets that this macro might create will be this name with a string suffix.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels#target-names">Name</a> | required |  |
| <a id="godot_pack-deps"></a>deps |  What the pack exports: godot_resources and add-ons, as on godot_resources. Applications reach the extensions and platform libraries of the pack's add-ons, the project's named ones included, through the pack.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `[]`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-deprecation"></a>deprecation |  Optional Bazel deprecation message for this authored pack.   | String; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | optional |  `""`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-entry_points"></a>entry_points |  Declared paths that reachable selection starts from in addition to the main scene, autoloads and other configured resources.   | List of strings | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-exec_compatible_with"></a>exec_compatible_with |  Execution platform constraints for this pack's export tools.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a>; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | optional |  `[]`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-exec_properties"></a>exec_properties |  Execution properties for this pack's actions.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `{}`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-export_options"></a>export_options |  Export preset options for this pack, as option name -> Godot literal string, for example `{"texture_format/etc2_astc": "true"}`. These are the options exporters and extensions' export plugins define in the preset's options section. binary_format/embed_pck and binary_format/architecture are set by the configured export platform and output layout.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-features"></a>features |  Bazel feature requests on export actions, distinct from Godot feature tags.   | List of strings | optional |  `[]`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-packing"></a>packing |  deps: every member of deps. reachable: what the project configuration, entry_points, extensions and runtime_deps of used targets reach through detected and declared references; fails where a reached file may load undeclared files.   | String | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-preset_settings"></a>preset_settings |  Supported preset fields as Godot literals: script_export_mode is 0, 1 or 2. Omitted fields retain Godot defaults. Custom features come from godot_project.custom_features. See [Godot configuration](../../configuration.md).   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-project"></a>project |  The godot_project whose configuration this pack exports.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">Label</a>; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | required |  |
| <a id="godot_pack-required_packs"></a>required_packs |  Packs whose resources this pack's references may use instead of packing them again; a path both declare must have the same source file. This is membership only, not runtime mounting or load order.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-settings"></a>settings |  Project settings for this export only, as section/property -> Godot literal string, for example `{"application/config/version": '"2.3.4"'}`. They replace the project's values in the exported configuration; imports, initialization and other packs keep the project's, so a change reruns only this export. Feature overrides such as `key.mobile` apply when the configured operating system or the project's custom features have the tag. Without an application/config/version entry here, a nonempty `--@autoload_rules_godot//godot:app_version` sets that setting.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-tags"></a>tags |  Conventional Bazel tags on this pack; internal helpers are additionally manual.   | List of strings; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | optional |  `[]`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-target_compatible_with"></a>target_compatible_with |  Bazel target compatibility constraints for this pack and its configured export.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `[]`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-testonly"></a>testonly |  <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#common.testonly">Inherited rule attribute</a>   | Boolean; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_pack-visibility"></a>visibility |  The visibility to be passed to this macro's exported targets. It always implicitly includes the location where this macro is instantiated, so this attribute only needs to be explicitly set if you want the macro's targets to be additionally visible somewhere else.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a>; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | optional |  |


<a id="godot_project"></a>

## godot_project

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot:defs.bzl", "godot_project")

godot_project(*, <a href="#godot_project-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_project-deps">deps</a>, <a href="#godot_project-autoload_overrides">autoload_overrides</a>, <a href="#godot_project-autoloads">autoloads</a>, <a href="#godot_project-context_files">context_files</a>, <a href="#godot_project-custom_features">custom_features</a>,
              <a href="#godot_project-deprecation">deprecation</a>, <a href="#godot_project-exec_compatible_with">exec_compatible_with</a>, <a href="#godot_project-exec_properties">exec_properties</a>, <a href="#godot_project-features">features</a>, <a href="#godot_project-main_scene">main_scene</a>, <a href="#godot_project-project_file">project_file</a>,
              <a href="#godot_project-setting_overrides">setting_overrides</a>, <a href="#godot_project-settings">settings</a>, <a href="#godot_project-settings_from_flags">settings_from_flags</a>, <a href="#godot_project-tags">tags</a>, <a href="#godot_project-target_compatible_with">target_compatible_with</a>,
              <a href="#godot_project-testonly">testonly</a>, <a href="#godot_project-visibility">visibility</a>)
</pre>

Declare the configuration context of a product: its project.godot, settings,
autoloads, main scene and the add-ons it names.

The project holds no resources. Every operation that runs Godot, such as
godot_pack, godot_run or godot_test, names a project and the
resources it works on; each resources target imports once under the project's
configuration, and every operation of the project for the same target platform
reuses that import. Settings that reach imports are the project's own, filtered by
the import purpose: the main scene, autoloads, settings naming files, keys outside
Godot's own sections and feature overrides the editor never applies stay out of
imports. The autoloads and
settings of the add-ons an operation contains merge with the project's per
operation, the project's last; conflicts require setting_overrides or
autoload_overrides. The add-ons the project names in deps are in every operation of
the project and import their parts under it like used add-ons.
A project is never testonly, also in a package with default_testonly: every resources
target imports under it, production resources included.

Example:
```starlark
godot_project(
    name = "project",
    project_file = "project.godot",
    main_scene = "main.tscn",
)

godot_pack(
    name = "pack",
    project = ":project",
    deps = [":main", ":textures"],
)
```

See [resource and configuration semantics](../../resources.md).

### Default outputs
- metadata (none): name the configuration context operations use; no build or run behavior

### Generated targets
- `{name}.named_addons` (metadata): The add-ons the project names, which the operations of the project reach without the project; not for direct use
  - purpose: analysis_boundary
  - visibility: caller

**ATTRIBUTES**


| Name  | Description | Type | Mandatory | Default |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_project-name"></a>name |  A unique name for this macro instance. Normally, this is also the name for the macro's main or only target. The names of any other targets that this macro might create will be this name with a string suffix.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels#target-names">Name</a> | required |  |
| <a id="godot_project-deps"></a>deps |  The add-ons the project names: those no content of its operations uses, such as an editor-only add-on with editor tooling, extensions every operation loads, and every add-on whose importer the project's content needs. Every operation of the project contains them, and they import their parts under the project like used add-ons. Their importer_suffixes and import_settings apply to the project's imports. godot_addon, godot_extension and godot_cc_extension targets.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-autoload_overrides"></a>autoload_overrides |  Explicitly replace conflicting autoload contributions of add-ons.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-autoloads"></a>autoloads |  Autoload name to res:// path, optionally prefixed with '*' for a singleton; conflicts require explicit overrides. An operation whose resources lack the script leaves the autoload out; a pack without required_packs and a source run fail instead.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-context_files"></a>context_files |  Single-file target to resource path of files bound to the context itself, such as an application icon a setting names.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: Label -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-custom_features"></a>custom_features |  The build settings whose values are the project's Godot custom features, such as bazel_skylib's string_flag (its value) and bool_flag (its name when true); its packs and source runs have them. | <a id="godot_project-exec_properties"></a>exec_properties |  <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#common.exec_properties">Inherited rule attribute</a>   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-features"></a>features |  <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#common.features">Inherited rule attribute</a>   | List of strings | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-main_scene"></a>main_scene |  Resource path of the main scene, with optional res:// prefix. An operation whose resources lack it leaves it out; a pack without required_packs and a source run fail instead.   | String | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-project_file"></a>project_file |  Declared project.godot file used as the base configuration.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">Label</a> | required |  |
| <a id="godot_project-setting_overrides"></a>setting_overrides |  Explicitly replace conflicting setting contributions of add-ons.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-settings"></a>settings |  section/property -> Godot literal string. Every setting the import purpose keeps affects every import of the project.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/rules/lib/core/dict">Dictionary: String -> String</a> | optional |  `None`  |

| <a id="godot_project-target_compatible_with"></a>target_compatible_with |  <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#common.target_compatible_with">Inherited rule attribute</a>   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-testonly"></a>testonly |  <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#common.testonly">Inherited rule attribute</a>   | Boolean; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | optional |  `None`  |
| <a id="godot_project-visibility"></a>visibility |  The visibility to be passed to this macro's exported targets. It always implicitly includes the location where this macro is instantiated, so this attribute only needs to be explicitly set if you want the macro's targets to be additionally visible somewhere else.   | <a href="https://bazel.build/concepts/labels">List of labels</a>; <a href="https://bazel.build/reference/be/common-definitions#configurable-attributes">nonconfigurable</a> | optional |  |
